newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Italrating in partnership with DCR of U.S..
newsitem.headline: Italy's Italrating in partnership with DCR of U.S..

text.p: Italrating, Italy's first credit rating agency set up a year ago, said it is joining forces with Duff & Phelps Credit Rating Co (DCR), which will take a 30 percent stake, as well as taking in new Italian partners.
Gianfranco Imperatori, chairman of Italrating and of Mediocredito Centrale SpA, up to now the majority shareholder, and managing director Marco Cecchi de' Rossi gave the details at a news conference.

Alongside the new U.S. shareholder, also coming in are Italian publisher Il Sole 24 Ore with 10 percent, the Associazione Nazionale fra le Banche Popolari (3.33 pct), and the Consiglio Nazionale dei Ragionieri e Periti Commerciali (1 pct). Mediocredito's stake will fall to 30 percent from 42.
The new alliance with DCR is considered to be strategic and could generate important synergies for Italrating in the face of strong competition from foreign rating agencies, Cecchi de' Rossi said.

"Our business is based on reputation. We have a one-year history but DCR has 60 years of experience and ranks among the four international agencies recognised by the Securities and Exchange Commission," he said.
Chicago-based DCR is known mainly in the U.S. and Japan but is also present with joint ventures in 15 countries in South America and Asia, an Italrating statement said.

The agreement foresees the exclusive use of the DCR name on the Italian market, with domestic ratings signed Italrating-DCR and foreign ratings requested by Italian groups signed DCR, Cecchi de' Rossi said.
DCR, which began extending its activities in Europe in 1994 when it opened a London office, said the link up with Italrating would reinforce its competitiveness.
"We have chosen Italy because we believe it to be a market with great potential," said Ernest T. Elsner, DCR Executive Vice President.
